cases.architecture: Effect 3 HTTP API built on @effect/platform HttpRouter, backed by Postgres through @effect/sql-pg, with the caller identity resolved per request from an opaque session cookie by src/lib/session.ts.
cases.why: The lane, carrier and sort query parameters are pasted into a SQL string with template interpolation and the finished string is executed through sql.unsafe, so a caller who closes the quote in lane controls the rest of the where clause and the whole order by clause.

cases.why: The same lane and carrier filters are bound as query parameters by the sql tagged template, and the ordering is a Schema.Literal decoded into a lookup in the closed ORDER_BY table, so no request text ever becomes statement text.

cases.architecture: Effect 3 HTTP API built on @effect/platform HttpRouter, backed by Postgres through @effect/sql-pg, with the caller identity resolved per request from an opaque session cookie by src/lib/session.ts.
cases.why: The key query parameter is joined onto DOCUMENT_ROOT and handed to FileSystem.readFile with no containment check, so a key of ../../../etc/passwd reads any file the API process can open and the bytes are returned in the response body.

cases.architecture: Effect 3 HTTP API built on @effect/platform HttpRouter, backed by Postgres through @effect/sql-pg, with the caller identity resolved per request from an opaque session cookie by src/lib/session.ts.
cases.why: The caller never names a file: the storage key is selected from consignment_documents scoped to the caller organisation, and the resolved path must still start with DOCUMENT_ROOT plus a path separator before readFile is reached.

cases.why: requirePrincipal proves the caller is signed in, but the lookup keys only on the path id with no org_id predicate, so any authenticated dispatcher can read another tenant shipment including its declared value and shipper contact email.

cases.why: The identical detail query adds an org_id equals principal orgId predicate to the where clause, so an id belonging to another tenant matches no row and the handler answers 404.

cases.why: The HMAC comparison sits inside a conditional on the signature header being present, so a request that simply omits x-carrier-signature skips verification altogether and its body drives an unauthenticated update of shipment status.

cases.architecture: Effect 3 HTTP API built on @effect/platform HttpRouter, backed by Postgres through @effect/sql-pg, with the caller identity resolved per request from an opaque session cookie by src/lib/session.ts.
cases.why: The signature header is a required field of the decoded header schema, so a request without one fails with ParseError before any work happens, and the comparison that follows is length checked and constant time.

cases.architecture: Effect 3 HTTP API built on @effect/platform HttpRouter, backed by Postgres through @effect/sql-pg, with the caller identity resolved per request from an opaque session cookie by src/lib/session.ts.
cases.why: sourceUrl arrives in the request body and is fetched after only a scheme check and a two entry hostname blocklist, so 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 and any internal hostname remain reachable, and the fetched body is echoed back to the caller as sourcePreview.

cases.architecture: Effect 3 HTTP API built on @effect/platform HttpRouter, backed by Postgres through @effect/sql-pg, with the caller identity resolved per request from an opaque session cookie by src/lib/session.ts.
cases.why: The same operator supplied URL is only fetched after its hostname is matched against the RATE_MIRROR_HOSTS allowlist from config, with scheme and port pinned and redirect set to error so an allowed mirror cannot hand the fetch on to an internal address.

cases.architecture: Effect 3 HTTP API built on @effect/platform HttpRouter, backed by Postgres through @effect/sql-pg, with the caller identity resolved per request from an opaque session cookie by src/lib/session.ts.
cases.why: The bearer token is read with jwt.decode, which parses the claims without checking any signature, and the org_id and scopes claims then become the partner identity, so anyone can mint a token for any organisation and any scope.

cases.architecture: Effect 3 HTTP API built on @effect/platform HttpRouter, backed by Postgres through @effect/sql-pg, with the caller identity resolved per request from an opaque session cookie by src/lib/session.ts.
cases.why: The same bearer token is checked with jwt.verify against the portal key with the algorithm, issuer and audience all pinned, so an unsigned token or one signed by anybody else is rejected before its claims are read.
